title: Office plant care and decor guidelines
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This page documents the recommended care, placement, and procurement guidelines for office plants and low-effort decor in Redwood Inference offices. The goal is to maintain a safe, healthy workplace, reduce allergens and pest risk, and ensure plants support wellbeing and culture without creating maintenance burden.

Scope:
- Applies to all shared indoor office spaces, meeting rooms, and communal areas in Redwood-managed offices.
- Does not cover employee personal desk plants (see "Personal desk plants" section).

Principles:
- Low-maintenance: prioritize species that tolerate office lighting and intermittent watering.
- Safety-first: avoid plants with known toxic sap or excessive shedding in high-traffic areas.
- Inclusive: accommodate allergies and scent sensitivities; avoid highly fragrant plants in shared spaces.
- Aesthetic coherence: plants and decor should be neutral and consistent with brand colors where practical.

Daily care checklist (facilities team):
1) Morning quick-check (mon-fri): inspect high-traffic common area plants for wilting, standing water, or pests.
2) Watering: follow the plant-specific schedule (see table below); avoid overwatering. Use saucers to prevent leaks.
3) Clean leaves monthly: wipe dust buildup to keep plants healthy and improve air quality.
4) Report issues: log major problems in #facilities with a photo and location.

Watering schedule by plant type (general guidance):
- Snake plant (Sansevieria): water every 4–6 weeks. Low light tolerant.
- ZZ plant (Zamioculcas zamiifolia): water every 4–6 weeks. Very low maintenance.
- Pothos/Devil's ivy: water every 10–14 days; trim vines if they encroach on walkways.
- Spider plant: water every 10–14 days; prefers bright, indirect light.
- Peace lily: water every 7–10 days; avoid placement where pollen may bother coworkers.
- Succulents/Cacti: water every 3–6 weeks depending on season.

Placement and safety guidelines:
- Do not place plants where they block egress, fire extinguishers, electrical panels, or sensors.
- Avoid hanging plants directly over desks where drips could occur.
- Ensure pots have trays; mopping and carpet damage incidents have previously come from unchecked overflow.
- Do not place heavily-shedding plants in meeting rooms or near shared keyboards and equipment.
- Plants with known mild-to-high toxicity (e.g., philodendron, oleander) are not allowed in common areas.

Personal desk plants (employee-owned):
- Allowed but must be maintained by the owner. If a plant becomes a nuisance (pests, mold, water damage) facilities may request removal.
- Use a waterproof tray and keep a small saucer under the pot.
- Notify facilities in case of spider/ant/pest sightings so coordinated treatment can occur.

Procurement and requests:
- To request a new plant or replacement, file a request in the Facilities request form (link in sidebar) with: proposed location, desired plant type (if known), and any accessibility concerns.
- Facilities maintains a small budget for replacements. For larger decorative refreshes, submit a ticket to People Ops with proposed spend and rationale.
- Preferred vendors: local nurseries and the approved vendor list (see Facilities vendor doc).

Decor guidelines (small items accompanying plants):
- Pots and stands should be neutral (matte blacks, grays, natural wood) unless coordinated as part of a themed refresh.
- No scented candles or oil diffusers in shared areas.
- Avoid porous pots that retain moisture directly against furniture; use trays and felt pads under stands.

Maintenance cadence and ownership:
- Facilities: weekly checklists, monthly leaf-clean, quarterly plant health review.
- People Ops: budget approvals, large refresh planning, and accommodation handling for allergies/sensitivities.
- Teams may volunteer to sponsor plants in their area (signup through People Ops); volunteer teams are responsible for basic watering on a shared rota.

Pest and allergy procedures:
- If pests (aphids, spider mites) are detected, quarantine the plant and notify #facilities immediately. Do not attempt over-the-counter pesticide sprays without coordination.
- For allergy complaints, People Ops will identify nearby plants and offer relocation/removal options. We prioritize non-confrontational resolutions and temporary workarounds (e.g., moving desks).

Exceptions and accommodations:
- If an individual requires a scent-free or plant-free workspace for medical reasons, People Ops will provide reasonable accommodation, including relocation or desk shields if needed.

- Facilities request form: /forms/facilities-request (internal link)
